# The Physics of Baseball

> > Comprehensive research on baseball physics including aerodynamics, bat-ball collisions, and equipment performance by Professor Alan Nathan at the University of Illinois.

This site serves as a central hub for scientific research on baseball mechanics, featuring studies on ball flight trajectories, bat performance testing, hitting mechanics, and collaborations with organizations like USA Baseball and NCAA. The research combines experimental data from systems like TrackMan and Statcast with theoretical physics models.

## Key Topics

- baseball aerodynamics
- Magnus force and drag
- bat-ball collision physics
- exit velocity and launch angle
- TrackMan and Statcast data
- non-wood bat performance
- batted ball analysis
- sweet spot mechanics
- torpedo bat research
- NCAA and USA Baseball standards
- hitting mechanics
- baseball flight trajectories
- equipment evolution
- visual perception in batting

## Core Research

- [The Physics of Baseball](https://baseball.physics.illinois.edu/): Homepage featuring baseball physics research by Alan Nathan at U. Illinois
- [Baseball Aerodynamics](https://baseball.physics.illinois.edu/aero.html): Aerodynamics research on Magnus force, drag, and Statcast trajectory data

## Historical Context & Pioneers

- [Baseball - Gold Glove Page](https://baseball.physics.illinois.edu/evolution.html): Historical evolution of baseball equipment and rule changes since 1800s
- [The Physics of Baseball - Pioneers of the Field](https://baseball.physics.illinois.edu/baseball-researchers.html): Profiles of baseball physics pioneers including Lyman Briggs and research

## Resources & References

- [Physics of Baseball - Miscellaneous Links](https://baseball.physics.illinois.edu/links.html): Curated links to baseball analytics resources, HITf/x, and research tools
